chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr al-Bazanti narrated from ʿAbd al-Karim ibn ʿAmr al-Khathʿami from Zurarah from Abu Jaʿfar عليه السلام, and Musa ibn Bakr from Zurarah from Abu Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

If a man is reported dead to his family, or they inform her that he has divorced her, and she observes the ʿiddah and then marries, then her husband comes afterward, the first has more right to her than this latter one, whether the latter consummated with her or did not consummate. And she is entitled from the latter to the mahr for what he lawfully enjoyed of her private part.
And ʿAbd al-Karim added in his hadith: and it is not for the latter ever to marry her again.

key_terms.أَحَقُّ بِهَا: has greater legal right to her
key_terms.اسْتَحَلَّ: lawfully enjoyed or made permissible through marriage

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a missing husband returns after his wife completed her ʿiddah and remarried?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about a woman who remarries after being informed that her husband died or divorced her, only for the first husband to later return. The ruling states that the first husband remains more entitled to the marriage bond, while the second husband owes the mahr for the lawful marital access that occurred. The added wording further states that the second husband may never marry her again.
